My research interests lie at the intersection of environmental economics, development economics, and impact evaluation. I primarily study land-use change, environmental policy enforcement, and the socio-economic and health co-benefits of conservation policies, with a strong regional focus on the Brazilian Amazon.

------------------------------------------------------------------------


-   **Explaining compliance with voluntary sustainability standards: A case study from Colombia's coffee belt** (2025)\
    Paulo Mortara Batistic, Thomas Dietz, Jan Börner, & Yannic Rudá Damm.\
    *Sustainable Development*, 33(1), 1417-1440.\
    [Publisher Link](https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.3189)

-   **Health benefits of reduced deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon** (2024)\
    Yannic Damm, Jan Börner, Nicolas Gerber, & Britaldo Soares Filho.\
    *Communications Earth & Environment*, 5(1), 693.\
    [Publisher Link](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-024-01840-7)

-   **Beyond Deforestation Reductions: Public Disclosure, Land-Use Change and Commodity Sourcing** (2024)\
    Yannic Damm, Elías Cisneros, & Jan Börner.\
    *World Development*, 175, 106481.\
    [Publisher Link](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.worlddev.2023.106481)

-   **SDGs trade‐offs associated with voluntary sustainability standards: A case study from the coffee sector in Costa Rica** (2024)\
    Karla Rubio‐Jovel, Jorge Sellare, Yannic Damm, & Thomas Dietz.\
    *Sustainable Development*, 32(1), 917–39.\
    [Publisher Link](https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.2701)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Working Papers

-   **Balancing Growth and Conservation: The Economic Impact of Environmental Enforcement in the Brazilian Amazon** (2025)\
    Yannic Damm, Gustavo Magalhães de Oliveira, & Jan Börner.\
    *Available at SSRN 5898282*.\
    [SSRN Working Paper Link](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5898282)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Media & Outreach

-   **Podcast:** [Rainforest conservation is bad for the economy!?](https://www.uni-bonn.de/en/news/rainforest-conservation-is-bad-for-the-economy) (2026)\
    A discussion on the relationship between rainforest conservation and the economic, health outcomes, and crime. With Gustavo Magalhães de Oliveira on the University of Bonn's *Hypothese* podcast.

-   **News Article:** Our paper "Health Benefits of Reduced Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon" in *Communications Earth & Environment* gathered some media attention. There was a press release by the [University of Bonn](https://www.uni-bonn.de/en/news/224-2024?set_language=en) and later the publication was covered by the [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/brazil-amazon-stop-deforestation-wildfire-public-health-v2/a-70845382) and Brazilian news outlets [O Globo](https://oglobo.globo.com/brasil/minas-gerais/noticia/2024/11/18/controle-do-desmatamento-na-amazonia-reduz-internacoes-e-mortes-por-doencas-respiratorias-diz-estudo-da-ufmg.ghtml) and [Agência Pública](https://apublica.org/nota/queda-no-desmatamento-da-amazonia-evitou-internacoes-por-doencas-respiratorias-diz-estudo/).

-   **Blogpost:** [Can public scrutiny make supply chains more sustainable?](https://iap.unido.org/articles/can-public-scrutiny-make-supply-chains-more-sustainable) (2024)\
    A summary of our paper "Beyond Deforestation Reductions: Public Disclosure, Land-Use Change and Commodity Sourcing" in *World Development* on the evidence from Brazilian municipalities which suggests that reputational risk exposure can reduce deforestation and intensify agriculture. With Elías Cisneros & Jan Börner on the United Nations Industrial Development Organization’s Industrial Analytics Platform.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
